Adam Bari
416 Drake Street, Boston, MA
Home: 967-1111  Cell: 439-000
madamiamadam@youremail.com


Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the position of Web Content Editor with “Never Odd Or Even” Publishing.

I found your job ad in the Boston Job Fair this morning. Since I am a freelance writer/editor with blog and social media experience, I truly believe I am a strong candidate for the job posting offered in your company.

As you can see in the attached resume, I hold a BA degree in Communications and Creative Writing from Boston University. I started my career as a reporter for a college magazine. I, then, began working as an editor for a small magazine. I transitioned into a web editor for the online version shortly after. My last experience was working for an independent paper and award-winning magazine called “The News Gazette”. These jobs taught me that editing web content is distinctly different from editing print content. My other duties included writing of feature articles for the website, managing content, and selling ad space.

Apart from my experience, I possess great verbal and writing skills with the ability to proofread and edit content in a timely manner so it is ready to be published. I can find any grammatical and spelling errors and have the ability to ensure content matches the writing style adopted by the company.

I am an organized and motivated individual who is committed and passionate about what I do. I am able to quickly adapt to new policies and procedures. I have a positive team player attitude with excellent interpersonal skills and always welcome opportunities to upgrade my knowledge and skills.

I would enjoy the opportunity to meet with you personally in order to discuss how my skills enable me to make a valuable contribution to your company.

Thank you for your time and consideration of my application.

Sincerely,

Adam Bari

Past Simple Tense vs. Present Simple Tense
When you write a resume, it is common to use a mixture of tenses. You can use the past and  present.
You use the Simple Present tense to talk about permanent situations or about things that happen regularly.

• Since I am a freelance writer/editor with blog and social media experience, I truly believe I am a strong candidate for the job posting offered in your company.
  • I hold a BA degree in Communications and Creative Writing from Boston University.
  • I am an organized and motivated individual who is committed and passionate about what I do.
  • I have a positive team player attitude with excellent interpersonal skills and always welcome opportunities to upgrade my knowledge and skills.
You use the Simple Past tense to talk about many kinds of past events: short, quickly finished actions, longer situations and repeated events.

• I found your job ad in the Boston Job Fair this morning.
  • I started my career as a reporter for a college magazine.
  • I began working as an editor for a small magazine.
  • These jobs taught me that editing web content is distinctly different from editing print content.
Cover Letter Expressions

A Cover Letter is a letter you send along with your resume. It is considered to be the first official contact between an employer and a potential employee. Therefore, you need to make sure it is well-written. Here are some phrases and expressions you can use when writing a Cover Letter.
1. Say that you would like to apply
I am applying for the position of (name of the position) with (company's name).
2. Say where you found out about the job

I found your job ad in (name) (when)
I found your job ad in the Boston Job Fair this morning.
3. Say why you are qualified for the job.
<span class="italic">Since I am a (job) with (describe experience) blog and social media experience, I truly believe I am a strong candidate for the job posting offered in your company.
<span class="italic">Since I am a freelance writer/editor with blog and social media experience, I truly believe I am a strong candidate for the job posting offered in your company.
<span class="italic">As you can see in the attached resume, I hold a (name of degree) from (name of university).
<span class="italic">I started my career as a/an (describe position) for (place/company)
<span class="italic">My other duties included (describe other things you did)
<span class="italic">Apart from my experience, I possess (describe qualities and strengths) with the ability to (describe what you can do for the company)
4. Say you can provide more information if necessary.
<span class="italic">I would enjoy the opportunity to meet with your personally in order to discuss how my skills enable me to make a valuable contribution to your company.
5. Say how thankful you are.
<span class="italic">Thank you for your time and consideration of my application.
